title: Chip on a Breadboard
description: Run a sketch on a bare ATmega328P chip — a whole Arduino made from a chip and four small parts.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × ATmega328P chip, 1 × 16 MHz crystal, 2 × 22 pF capacitor, 1 × 10 kΩ resistor, 1 × 220 Ω resistor, 1 × LED, and some jumper wires.
Push the ATmega328P chip in across the middle gap, the notch (the little half-moon dent) on the left.
hints: With the notch on the left, pin 1 is bottom-left. Pins 1–14 run left to right along the bottom, 15–28 come back along the top.
Press gently on both ends so all 28 legs go in straight.
steps.goal: Put the chip on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. Chip pin 7 (VCC) → that same row.
hints: VCC is the chip's power in.
Count from pin 1 (bottom-left): along the bottom to 14, then back along the top from 15 on the right.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. Chip pin 8 (GND) → that same row.
hints: The chip's ground.
Count from pin 1 (bottom-left): along the bottom to 14, then back along the top from 15 on the right.

steps.clip: Run a wire from chip pin 20 (AVCC) to the red + row.
hints: AVCC powers the chip's analog side — it needs 5V too.
Count from pin 1 (bottom-left): along the bottom to 14, then back along the top from 15 on the right.

steps.clip: Run a wire from chip pin 22 (GND) to the blue − row.
hints: The chip's second ground pin — connect both.
Count from pin 1 (bottom-left): along the bottom to 14, then back along the top from 15 on the right.

steps.clip: Push the 16 MHz crystal (the small silver can) in to the right of the chip, its two legs in two columns next to each other.
hints: The crystal is the chip's clock. It works either way round.
steps.goal: Put the crystal on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from chip pin 9 to the crystal's left leg.
hints: Chip pin 9 is the 9th leg from the left on the bottom row.
Either crystal leg is fine — it has no + or −.
steps.goal: Connect chip pin 9 to the crystal.

steps.clip: Run a wire from chip pin 10 to the crystal's right leg.
hints: Chip pin 10 is the 10th leg from the left on the bottom row.
Either crystal leg is fine — it has no + or −.
steps.goal: Connect chip pin 10 to the crystal.

steps.clip: Push a 22 pF capacitor (marked “22”) in: one leg in the same column as the crystal's left leg, the other leg two columns to the left.
hints: It helps the crystal start and keep a steady beat.
It works either way round.
steps.goal: Put a 22 pF capacitor on the crystal's left leg.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the capacitor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Each crystal leg gets its own 22 pF capacitor to GND.
steps.goal: Connect the capacitor's other leg to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 22 pF capacitor (marked “22”) in: one leg in the same column as the crystal's right leg, the other leg two columns to the right.
hints: It helps the crystal start and keep a steady beat.
It works either way round.
steps.goal: Put a 22 pF capacitor on the crystal's right leg.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the capacitor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Each crystal leg gets its own 22 pF capacitor to GND.
steps.goal: Connect the capacitor's other leg to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the same column as chip pin 1 (bottom-left), the other leg four columns to the left.
hints: Pin 1 is bottom-left, by the notch.
A resistor works either way round.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor on chip pin 1 (RESET).

steps.clip: Run a wire from the resistor's other leg to the red + row.
hints: RESET held at 5V lets the chip run. At GND it would restart.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into an empty part of the breadboard, its legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
steps.goal: Put the LED's resistor on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from chip pin 19 to one leg of the resistor.
hints: Chip pin 19 is the chip's digital pin 13 — the Blink pin.
It is on the top row.
steps.goal: Connect chip pin 19 to the resistor.

steps.clip: Put the LED in: the long leg in the same column as the resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is +. Backwards, the LED stays dark.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the LED's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: The short leg is −.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Nothing to upload: the chip already has Blink from the last level. Plug in the USB cable — the Uno only gives the chip power now. The LED on chip pin 19 blinks once a second. (A fresh chip? Program it first, as in the last level.)
